sections.title: SEO for education and training centers
sections.text: Someone looking for a course wants to know what they'll learn, who it's for, when it starts and how to register. Others search for a whole field or learning path before choosing a single program. We build clear pages for fields, learning paths and courses, and connect them so applicants find the information they need, without duplicates or conflicts between the in-person, live online and self-paced versions.

Field, path or course?
sections.title: Every level of learning gets its own page
sections.text: One learner may search for a whole field before they know a course name; another may search for a specific program and its dates. We distinguish between the field page, which presents the options; the learning path page, which sets out the order of study; and the course page, which holds the details needed to register. That way, users find what they want without lots of pages competing for the same description.

sections.label: Information that settles the decision
sections.title: What applicants need to know before registering
sections.text: When a provider offers the same course in person, live online or self-paced, we check whether each format really offers a different experience and content before deciding to give it its own page. Past dates are updated, and visitors find a suitable alternative instead of a form for a closed cohort.

sections.label: Measuring registrations
sections.title: From search to enrollment request
sections.text: We track the pages where an applicant's visit begins, then their move to the course details, the start of registration and the submitted application.

items.text: We don't treat reading an introductory article the same as an enrollment request; each plays a different role.
We explain our measurement tools and their limits clearly, and we don't credit registrations to SEO unless the channel or the form is tracked correctly.

sections.title: Questions about SEO for education and training

items.question: Does every course need its own page?
items.answer: Yes, for courses with real search demand and details that set them apart. Similar courses can be presented on a single learning path page, which is clearer for learners.

items.question: What happens when a course date has passed?
items.answer: We update the page with the next date if the course runs again, or point visitors to a suitable alternative instead of a form for a closed cohort.

items.question: How do you avoid duplicate versions of the same course?
items.answer: We create a separate page for the in-person or online format only when the content or experience genuinely differs, not just because the delivery format changes.

items.question: How do you measure registrations?
items.answer: We track registration starts and submitted applications from organic search for each course, as long as the form is connected to tracking.
